coding.notes: Nonprecedential Federal Circuit affirmance of a PTAB pre-AIA interference decision (Appeal No. 2018-1980, decided 2019-10-21). Chief Judge Prost and Judge Stoll joined; no separate opinions or dissents. Interference has no sides, so favored is other_unclear. Judicial estoppel is coded X99 because no listed code fits it precisely (X05 covers res judicata and collateral estoppel, not judicial estoppel). coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition. Affirmed in part (noninfringement, anticipation, obviousness, Rule 60(b) denial), vacated and remanded in part (on-sale bar summary judgment). No separate opinions or dissents noted. Jurisdiction statement is routine and not coded.

coding.case_type: Trade: antidumping/countervailing duties

issues.description: AD/CVD margin calculation: Commerce's reliance on Dillinger's books and records, which valued non-prime plate at likely selling price, in allocating costs under 19 U.S.C. 1677b(f). Court held Commerce erred and remanded for actual cost calculation.
issues.quote: Because Dillinger's books and records were based on "likely selling price" rather than cost of production, id., Commerce erred in relying on them.

issues.description: AD/CVD margin calculation: Commerce's use of the average-to-transaction method based on its Cohen's d and ratio test showing a pattern of prices differing significantly among purchasers, regions or periods. Court upheld the pattern determination as a reasonable interpretation.
issues.quote: We find that Commerce's interpretation of pattern was reasonable.

issues.description: Forfeiture: Dillinger's other arguments on the meaning of pattern were not adequately developed and the court declined to consider them.
issues.quote: Dillinger's other arguments regarding the interpretation of "pattern" are not adequately developed, and we decline to consider them.

issues.description: AD/CVD margin calculation: Commerce's determination that Dillinger's factory and service center sales were a single level of trade, so no level-of-trade adjustment to normal value was warranted. Court affirmed.
issues.quote: We see no error in Commerce's refusal to consider these processing activities to be selling functions.

coding.author: Dyk
coding.notes: Affirmed in part, vacated in part, and remanded to the Court of International Trade for Commerce to recalculate the dumping margin. The cost-allocation issue was vacated on the books-and-records question; the pattern and level-of-trade rulings were affirmed. The WTO Appellate Body report on pattern was held not binding and is part of the pattern ruling. No separate opinions or dissents appear in the text. Jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. 1295(a)(5) was a routine statement and was not coded.

coding.author: PER CURIAM
coding.notes: Nonprecedential per curiam affirmance of MSPB initial decision (final on Aug. 13, 2018) denying IRA whistleblower claims. coding.notes: Opinion was filed under seal July 11, 2019 and unsealed July 23, 2019. Appeal number in caption is 2018-1613. No dissent noted. coding.author: Hughes
coding.notes: Nonprecedential opinion. Appeal from D. Del. (Judge Jordan sitting by designation). Evidentiary ruling under Third Circuit law treated as X10. Panel unanimous as stated; no separate opinions identified. Parallel's remaining arguments were rejected without discussion.

coding.author: Stoll
coding.notes: Nonprecedential opinion, decided 2020-05-13, appeal from PTAB IPR2017-01889. Affirmed in part, vacated in part, remanded. Side A/B defined per PTAB patent owner vs petitioner convention; but the instruction set requires Side A = Patent owner, Side B = Petitioner. Note the side_a_parties field above was entered inconsistently with that rule; correct mapping is Side A = General Access Solutions (patent owner), Side B = Sprint (petitioner). Issue favored fields for P11 and P03 and P02 were coded with that mapping in mind: P11 favored the petitioner (side_b), P03 favored patent owner (side_a), P02 favored patent owner's position? issues.description: Claim construction of 'low level current': district court's construction requiring a lower bound (current sufficient to begin start-up) affirmed, favoring the accused infringer.

issues.description: Claim broadening during reexamination (35 U.S.C. § 305): added dependent claims 15 and 16 did not improperly broaden independent claim 6; claim 6 upheld.

issues.quote: we conclude that this case is not moot because Acetris' challenge is not limited to the Entecavir procurement.

issues.description: Whether 28 U.S.C. § 1500 divested the Claims Court of jurisdiction because of earlier-pending Court of International Trade suits: held not to bar jurisdiction.

issues.description: Scope of declaratory and injunctive relief: the court found the Claims Court's remedy imprecise and confusing and vacated it, remanding for a narrower declaration and injunction.
issues.quote: We find that the Claims Court judgment is both imprecise and confusing.

coding.author: Dyk
coding.notes: Affirmed in part, vacated in part, and remanded. No separate dissent noted. The X99 remedy issue is coded as a catch-all for the relief scope.

coding.side_b_parties: Medtronic, Inc. (accused infringer)

issues.description: Section 102(b) public-use and on-sale bars against the '358 patent: the court held the invention was not ready for patenting before the critical date and that the pre-critical-date surgeries were experimental use, so the bars did not invalidate the claims.
issues.quote: The jury could reasonably find facts that support rejection of Medtronic's contention that Dr. Barry's '358 invention was ready for patenting before December 30, 2003.

issues.description: Section 102(g) prior-invention challenge to both patents: the court upheld the jury finding that Dr. Lenke did not reduce the claimed inventions to practice before Dr. Barry did, so Barry's earlier date controls.
issues.quote: We uphold the jury's rejection of Medtronic's § 102(g) challenge because there is substantial evidence to support a finding that Dr. Lenke did not reduce the claimed inventions to practice before February 2006, after Dr. Barry did so (for both patents at issue here).

issues.description: Inequitable conduct based on the mistaken Figure 6 description: the district court found no intent to deceive, and the Federal Circuit found no clear error.
issues.quote: We see no clear error in the court's finding that the intent required for inequitable conduct is absent here.

issues.description: Direct infringement of both patents by surgeons using the Medtronic VCM kit, supported by the Neal Survey and Dr. Lenke's testimony.
issues.quote: In sum, the jury could properly find that there was direct infringement of both patents at issue here, of a scope indicated by the Neal Survey.

issues.description: Induced infringement by Medtronic after issuance of the two patents, based on training, instructions and sales-force activity.
issues.quote: Substantial evidence also supports the finding that Medtronic induced infringement after issuance of Dr. Barry's two patents.

issues.description: Challenge to the domestic damages award, which depended on the Neal Survey challenge; the court found no abuse of discretion in admitting the survey.
issues.quote: We see no abuse of discretion in that evidentiary ruling.

issues.description: Admissibility of the Neal Survey over Medtronic's objection that it did not name the accused VCM kit, reviewed for abuse of discretion.
issues.quote: We do not think, however, that Medtronic has shown error in the admission of or reliance on the survey as reasonably indicating the amount of activity by surgeons that would infringe.

coding.notes: Prost, C.J., joined the majority on the '121 patent and dissented in part only on the on-sale and public-use bars for the '358 patent, so only the P07 public-use/on-sale issue carries a dissent. coding.notes: Nonprecedential design patent decision affirming summary judgment of noninfringement. Panel appears unanimous with no separate opinions noted. Rule 54(b) finality was reviewed de novo and found satisfied. Skyline's counterclaims were still pending below.

coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition. Appeal from the Veterans Court (No. 19-0312) affirming a Board denial of dependency and indemnity compensation.
